root_cause.text: The packet length validation in rxe_rcv() only ensured the packet was at least header_size(pkt) bytes, failing to account for the attacker-controlled BTH pad field and the ICRC size that payload_size() subtracts, allowing a crafted short packet to cause payload_size() to underflow and pass an invalid negative value to the receive path.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states, "rxe_rcv() currently checks only that the incoming packet is at least header_size(pkt) bytes long before payload_size() is used. However, payload_size() subtracts both the attacker-controlled BTH pad field and RXE_ICRC_SIZE from pkt->paylen ... This means a short packet can still make payload_size() underflow even if it includes enough bytes for the fixed headers." The patch fixes this by changing the minimum length check to `header_size(pkt) + bth_pad(pkt) + RXE_ICRC_SIZE`.
